learning_outcomes.text: Understand the technologies of Hydraulic and Pneumatic systems.
Understand the functional properties of the elements included in pneumatic and hydraulic circuits.
Be able to select components for an application.
Be able to design hydraulic and pneumatic systems, following a specification.

syllabus_topics: Fluid Power systems: energy and power by fluids. Main application areas. Power systems.
Pneumatic systems technology: Compressed air: production, conditioning and distribution.
Actuators: types, properties, selection and sizing
Control valves: directional, pressure and flow control
ISO 1219 graphical representation of fluid power systems.
Hydraulic systems technology: Overall analysis of hydraulic systems applications
Actuators. Types, technology aspects, sizing. performance characteristics. Efficiency aspects.
Control valves: directional, pressure and flow control
Auxiliary components: filters and filtering, cooling, instrumentation.
Hydraulic circuit analysis, sizing and design.
teaching_methods: Tutorials for circuit analysis, sizing and design

assessment_methods.method: Mini written laboratory Test about pneumatics (TL1)
Mini written laboratory Test about Hydraulics (TL2)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written exam (EE) weighted 75%, and a distributed evaluation comprising two mini laboratory tests (TL1 and TL2) each weighted 12.5%. For approval, a minimum classification of 8.5 out of 20 is required in the written exam (EE). Non-attendance to any evaluation component results in a zero score for that component. Distributed assessment (TL1, TL2) is not subject to appeal or improvement, but the written exam (EE) is.
bibliography: Katharina Schmitz; Fundamentals of fluid power . ISBN: 978-3-8440-6306-6
